CIS1.name: Variable Name
CIS1.note: The variable name that replaces the CTDA's first argument. It trails a CTDA that uses a string parameter, and the CTDA's parameter 1 is then a very high value. [documented: xEdit wbDefinitionsFO4.pas, wbCTDAParam1StringToInt; observed: CIS1 follows a CTDA in INFO and PACK.]

CIS2.name: Variable Name
CIS2.note: The variable name that replaces the CTDA's second argument. It trails a CTDA that uses a string parameter. [documented: xEdit wbDefinitionsFO4.pas, wbCTDAParam1StringToInt; observed: CIS2 follows a CTDA in INFO.]

CTDA.name: Condition
CTDA.note: The condition reads as <Reference>.<Function>(<Param1>, <Param2>) <Operator> <Value>. [documented: xEdit wbDefinitionsFO4.pas, wbCTDA; observed: every one of the 101,882 CTDA subrecords in Fallout4.esm is exactly 32 bytes, so Run On, Reference and the trailing index are all present, as in Skyrim — Fallout's CTDA has only the first two of the three, and its last two fields are optional.]

struct.name: operator
struct.note: The upper 3 bits are the compare operator (0 = Equal to, 1 = Not equal to, 2 = Greater than, 3 = Greater than or equal to, 4 = Less than, 5 = Less than or equal to) and the lower 5 bits are flags: 0x01 = OR (otherwise conditions are ANDed together), 0x02 = Parameters (use aliases), 0x04 = Use global, 0x08 = Use Pack Data, 0x10 = Swap Subject and Target.

struct.name: comparison_value_raw
struct.note: The value the function result is compared against: a float, or a GLOB formid when the 0x04 Use global flag is set. Decoded as a raw u32.

struct.name: function
struct.note: The condition function's index. [documented: xEdit wbDefinitionsFO4.pas, wbCTDAFunctionToStr.]

struct.name: padding
struct.note: Padding. The bytes are unused but may be non-zero.

struct.name: parameter1_raw
struct.note: The first parameter: a number, or a formid when the function takes one. Zero when the function needs no parameter. A string parameter is a CIS1 subrecord following the CTDA instead.

struct.name: parameter2_raw
struct.note: The second parameter, same shape as the first. A string parameter is a CIS2 subrecord following the CTDA instead.

struct.name: run_on
struct.note: How the condition applies: 0 = Subject, 1 = Target, 2 = Reference (see the reference field), 3 = Combat Target, 4 = Linked Reference, 5 = Quest Alias, 6 = Package Data, 7 = Event Data. Always present in Fallout 4, as in Skyrim. [observed: 0 and 1 in the sampled CTDAs of Fallout4.esm.]

struct.name: reference_raw
struct.note: The reference the condition is about, when the run-on type is Reference. Zero when it is not.

struct.name: unknown2
struct.note: The index of the package data or quest alias to run on. -1 means 'none', and it is also used for other run-on types. [observed: -1 in every sampled CTDA of Fallout4.esm.]
